done.why: I had read a fair sample of the prose and the garden had only just opened up. I stopped there as a reader.

about: A retelling of Zork II. You start in a barrow, cross a cavern by a foot bridge, and reach a formal garden with a unicorn and a gazebo. The prose is dry and wry, and the lantern is a knowing nod to the first game.

ending.what: None reached. I stopped in the middle of the formal garden.

moments.note: The lantern is described as something that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
The ribbon on the unicorn is tied to be undone by somebody in particular, and the unicorn's look says I am not that somebody.
The bare 'You can't go that way' is flat next to the rest of the writing.
The place mat is thin enough to slide under most doors, which hints at a puzzle.
'go out' of the gazebo printed only the room name, with no description.

wished: To untie the ribbon or try to win the unicorn's trust
To see more of the garden and the bushes to the south

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: Wry, and it works as a wink to players who know the first game.

lines.line: The ribbon is tied in the sort of bow that is meant to be untied by somebody in particular, and the unicorn's look makes it plain that you are not the somebody.
lines.why: Characterful, and it sets up a puzzle without stating it.

lines.line: thin enough to slide under most doors, should you ever need to slide something under a door.
lines.why: A playful nudge at the puzzle.

fun.why: Small discoveries kept coming and the descriptions were pleasant to read.

engagement.why: The unicorn and its key made me want to go on.

difficulty.why: I met no obstacle in the short stretch I played, only one failed move.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork II places reworked with added detail, and Zork II's own newspaper text was kept.

prose.why: Dry humour and good added detail in the object descriptions. The room descriptions are the original text, and they are plainer.
